title: Check yourself: Templates, placement and instructions that hold up

questions.stem: A support tool inserts each customer message into a template. One customer's message contains the literal string `{{refund_limit}}`, which is also a variable of the template. What must the filling code do?

options.text: Escape the braces first, then rebuild the whole template from its original source
options.says: Ruled out because the page asks only to "Fill in one pass", with no step that rebuilds the template.

options.text: Rescan the filled template until no placeholder remains anywhere in the output
options.says: Ruled out because "never scan the result again" is the rule that keeps a customer's placeholder from being read as a template.

options.text: Delete curly braces from every incoming customer message before filling anything
options.says: Ruled out because the page's fix is a single pass, and a value "must come out as those characters", not as edited text.

options.text: Substitute every placeholder in one pass and keep what was typed untouched
options.says: The page says to "Replace every `{{name}}` once, from left to right, and never scan the result again", so data stays data.

origin.section: A template is a prompt with holes

questions.stem: A team keeps adding one sentence to the system prompt after every complaint, and answers to the original tasks now get worse. Which explanation fits the page?

options.text: Rules that matter become a small share of the text and compete
options.says: The page says the rules that matter are "a small share of the text" when a prompt "grows by accretion".

options.text: The model stops reading everything that follows the first paragraph
options.says: Ruled out because the mechanism described is that the model "weighs them against the thirty that do not", not that it stops reading.

options.text: The API refuses any system prompt that grows beyond a fixed size
options.says: Ruled out because the effect described is a change in behaviour: "If you find the model thinking more often than you'd like".

options.text: Each newer rule cancels the older ones, so the earlier rules are lost
options.says: Ruled out because the page's advice "Say a rule once, in one place, so that two lines cannot disagree" shows rules competing, not newer ones cancelling older ones.

questions.stem: A nightly job classifies thousands of ambiguous tickets with nobody watching. What should the prompt tell the model to do when a ticket allows two readings?

options.text: Ask the sender which meaning was intended before assigning any label
options.says: Ruled out because an interactive assistant "can ask, but one question at a time", which needs someone to answer.

options.text: Stop the whole run for every ticket and wait until a person gives an answer
options.says: Ruled out because "A nightly batch has nobody to answer", so waiting would never end.

options.text: Choose the more probable meaning and record that choice with the label
options.says: The page says that "A nightly batch has nobody to answer, so the prompt should tell the model to choose the likeliest reading and write the assumption in the output".

options.text: Return an empty label for the ticket so that no guess is ever made
options.says: Ruled out because the documented behaviour is to "state the assumption you made" and not to withhold a result.
